html:
Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is the main spy agency of Pakistan, run by the army. It was set up in 1948, soon after Partition, when the first Kashmir war showed Pakistan needed better military intelligence.

It became far more powerful in the 1980s, as the go-between for the CIA's program to arm the Afghan mujahideen. All weapons and money for the Afghan resistance passed through the ISI, which decided who got them, trained fighters in camps near the border and generally favoured Islamist groups such as Hekmatyar's Hizb-i-Islami. Pakistan's military ruler Zia ul-Haq saw an Afghanistan friendly to Pakistan as a defence against India.

After the Soviets left, the ISI kept backing Afghan clients, and was later accused of helping the Taliban. It also has a long record in Kashmir.
sum: Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is the main spy agency of Pakistan, run by the army. It was set up in 1948, soon after Partition, when the first Kashmir war showed Pakistan needed better military intelligence.
